subject.title: Session→model/runtime binding drift persists across doctor --fix --deep because the repair's provider-ownership registry is missing the literal id "openai"

question: Should literal `openai` auto session route state be owned by the Codex doctor contract, by a new OpenAI provider doctor contract, or by provider-agnostic stale-auto route repair?
rationale: Literal `openai` is both the canonical OpenAI provider and the route used by Codex-backed OpenAI runtime paths, so automation should not choose the permanent ownership boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
options.body: Add OpenAI-side doctor ownership for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and tests for auto fallback cleanup, leaving Codex ownership focused on Codex ids, runtime ids, and legacy `openai-codex` aliases.

options.title: Codex owns app-server OpenAI routes
options.body: Add `openai` to the Codex doctor route-state owner if maintainers define OpenAI model turns through the Codex app-server as Codex-owned for cleanup.

options.title: Make stale auto cleanup generic
options.body: Clear stale auto model overrides when the configured route no longer includes the override provider, without relying on a plugin owner for canonical provider ids.

recommendation.title: OpenAI owns canonical provider state
recommendation.body: Add OpenAI-side doctor ownership for `providerIds: ["openai"]` and tests for auto fallback cleanup, leaving Codex ownership focused on Codex ids, runtime ids, and legacy `openai-codex` aliases.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the prior merged doctor/Codex route-state repair work and is the strongest available owner-boundary signal for this path.
